![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/144259aa150936de0e3425c13f953da0833d87c2aba1304aa39b3c47fda03550.png)

The region enclosed by the curve $x=6\sqrt{y}+1,$ the horizontal line $y=1,$  the horizontal line $y=0,$ and the vertical line $x=-1$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=-1$, as shown above. Find the volume of the resulting solid.
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=1$ along the $y$-axis.

To determine which is the left function and which is the right, let's draw our horizontal arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/8a17502c300fae56e9f2e1706d23a3e5a7d3233eebff9a77958d117a0135adb0.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=-1,$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=6\sqrt{y}+1.$

Therefore, the volume of the resulting solid is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{right function})-(\text{left function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(6\sqrt{y}+1)-(-1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(6\sqrt{y}+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(36y+24\sqrt{y}+4)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(36y+24{y}^{1/2}+4)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {(36\cdot \frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}+24\cdot \frac{2}{3}{y}^{3/2}+4y)|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\pi [(18(1)^{2}+16(1)^{3/2}+4(1))-0] \\  & =38\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
